source_name: CBCG — Mikrokreditne finansijske institucije (register of MFIs)
why_relevant: Covers the non-bank credit tier (MFIs, and the broader 'pružaoci finansijskih usluga' branch: leasing, factoring, credit-guarantee) — actors frequently missed when only banks/PSPs are tracked.

source_name: CBCG — Centralni registar transakcionih računa pravnih lica i preduzetnika (CRTR)
why_relevant: Central register of transaction accounts of legal entities/entrepreneurs; indirectly reveals which banks hold which corporate account relationships and publishes account-population statistics.

source_name: CBCG — Prinudna naplata: podaci o blokiranim pravnim licima i preduzetnicima
why_relevant: Enforcement register published as downloadable PDF and Excel with periodic cut-off dates — machine-readable, longitudinal credit-distress dataset, plus a searchable debtor lookup.

source_name: CBCG — Kreditni registar (Credit Registry) service pages
why_relevant: Defines which institutions are obliged reporters to the credit registry — an indirect but authoritative enumeration of regulated lenders, and a pointer to reporting rulebooks/deadlines.

source_name: Centralni registar privrednih subjekata (CRPS) — pretraga registra
why_relevant: National company register run under the Tax Administration. Resolves legal names, registration numbers, ownership and status for every bank, PSP, agent and fintech, and is the join key between CBCG registers and corporate data.

source_name: eFirma / IRMS portal (Poreska uprava) — business-entity register search
why_relevant: Newer Tax Administration front end to the same registry data; more likely than legacy crps.me to expose structured/JSON endpoints and to remain live as the legacy site is retired.

source_name: Registar stvarnih vlasnika (Beneficial Ownership Register), CRPS/eFirma
why_relevant: UBO register established 1 Aug 2021 under the AML/CFT law; the only official route to ultimate ownership of licensed financial institutions, agents and exchange offices, and a direct AML-supervision touchpoint.

source_name: Službeni list Crne Gore — official gazette archive and search
why_relevant: Authoritative publication of every law, decree and CBCG decision, with a searchable archive back to 1945 and a separate register of consolidated texts ('prečišćeni tekstovi'). It is the definitive date-of-entry-into-force and deadline source, and it preserves texts after ministry pages are taken down.

source_name: eUprava — e-participacija / javne rasprave (public consultation archive)
why_relevant: Central archive of public consultations on draft laws and strategies, each with a stated consultation window (typically 30 days). It is the canonical index of consultation deadlines and often keeps the draft after the ministry page is removed.

source_name: gov.me — Government/ministry news and consultation notices
why_relevant: Ministries (notably Ministarstvo finansija) publish consultation calls and deadlines as /clanak/ pages; these are the first public announcement and the URL pattern is stable and crawlable.

source_name: Agencija za nadzor osiguranja Crne Gore (Insurance Supervision Agency) — registers
why_relevant: Registers of insurers, branches of foreign insurers, brokers, agents and agencies — the bancassurance-adjacent actor list, and the third supervisory authority whose consultations and deadlines run in parallel to CBCG's.

source_name: Registar zaloga Crne Gore (Pledge Register) via sudovi.me
why_relevant: Public register of pledges over movable assets — reveals which lenders are taking security over what, i.e. an indirect map of secured-lending activity by bank and MFI, plus a judicial-branch data source distinct from CBCG.

source_name: Komora javnih izvršitelja Crne Gore — imenik izvršitelja i propisi
why_relevant: Official directory of public bailiffs (the enforcement channel banks use for retail/SME debt) plus a curated 'propisi' and 'načelni pravni stavovi' section that archives enforcement-law texts and binding legal positions.

source_name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine — snapshots of cbcg.me, gov.me, euprava.gov.me, skupstina.me
why_relevant: The archival backstop for this cell: Montenegrin regulator and ministry sites are frequently reorganised (cbcg.me already shows mangled legacy paths in search indexes, and gov.me migrated from older portals). Wayback preserves consultation drafts, deadline notices and superseded register versions after removal, and supports point-in-time diffing of register membership.

source_name: NATLEX (ILO) — Montenegro legislation records with archived Službeni list PDFs
why_relevant: International body that mirrors Montenegrin Official Gazette texts as durable PDFs — a fallback copy when sluzbenilist.me paywalls or reorganises an issue.

source_name: registarfirmi.me — commercial company-profile aggregator (Montenegro)
why_relevant: Third-party mirror of CRPS company data with clean per-entity URLs; useful for fast name resolution and alias discovery when the official portals are down or rate-limited. Not authoritative — always reconcile against CRPS.

source_name: MONEYVAL (Council of Europe) — Montenegro country evaluation page
why_relevant: MONEYVAL is the binding external AML/CFT assessor for Montenegro. Its 5th-round Mutual Evaluation Report (Dec 2023) and enhanced follow-up reports (latest adopted at the 70th plenary, 15-18 Dec 2025, published Jan 2026) carry dated re-reporting obligations (Montenegro to report back within one year) that drive Montenegrin legislative and supervisory deadlines for banks, PSPs and DNFBPs.

source_name: FATF Global Network — Montenegro country hub (mirrors MONEYVAL MER/FUR)
why_relevant: FATF republishes the MONEYVAL Montenegro Mutual Evaluation Report (2023) and Follow-Up Reports (2025) in stable, machine-fetchable PDF form, plus technical-compliance rating tables per FATF Recommendation. Ratings deltas are the single cleanest quantitative signal of Montenegrin AML regulatory change affecting banks and PSPs.

source_name: IMF — Montenegro country page (Article IV consultations, staff reports, press releases)
why_relevant: Annual Article IV consultation is the most reliable dated external assessment of Montenegro's banking sector. The 2025 Article IV (Board concluded 18 Nov 2025, PR 25/381) addressed rapid private-sector credit growth, cash loans, real-estate exposure, supervision quality, AML enforcement and SEPA integration — all directly bearing on bank regulation and supervisory tightening.

source_name: IMF/World Bank FSAP — Montenegro Financial Sector Assessment Program technical notes
why_relevant: FSAP technical notes (banking supervision, stress testing, crisis management/resolution, AML) generate multi-year recommendation lists that Montenegrin authorities then implement; subsequent Article IVs explicitly track FSAP-recommendation implementation, making the FSAP the anchor document for a dated reform backlog.

source_name: European Commission — Montenegro Enlargement Report (SWD), Chapters 4, 9, 24, 32
why_relevant: The annual Country Report is the most granular external audit of Montenegro's financial-services acquis alignment (Ch.9 Financial services, Ch.4 Free movement of capital incl. AML, Ch.32 Financial control). It states, chapter by chapter, what remains to be transposed — effectively an English-language forward regulatory calendar for banks and PSPs.

source_name: European Commission — Montenegro accession financial package / negotiating framework communications
why_relevant: The June 2026 financial package communication for Montenegro's accession negotiations sets the fiscal and chapter-closing timetable that conditions when financial-services acquis chapters must be provisionally closed — an upstream driver of regulatory deadlines.

source_name: ECB Banking Supervision — MoU with the Central Bank of Montenegro / international cooperation register
why_relevant: The 2018 ECB(SSM)–CBCG Memorandum of Understanding governs supervisory information exchange for EU banking-group subsidiaries in Montenegro (the market is dominated by EU-parent banks). New or amended MoUs signal changes in consolidated supervision and in how EU-level supervisory expectations reach Montenegrin subsidiaries.

source_name: EBA — third-country equivalence, professional-secrecy assessments and SEE Memorandum of Cooperation
why_relevant: EBA equivalence guidelines determine whether the CBCG's confidentiality regime is treated as EU-equivalent (Montenegro assessed positively), which gates supervisory-college participation and cross-border data flows. The 2015 Vienna-Initiative SEE Memorandum of Cooperation, to which Montenegro is a signatory, is the operating framework.

source_name: European Payments Council — SEPA geographical scope, scheme country list and adherence calendar
why_relevant: The EPC sets the binding operational dates for Montenegrin PSP adherence to SCT, SCT Inst and SDD (adherence enabled from April 2025; Operational Readiness Date 5 Oct 2025). The versioned 'EPC List of SEPA Scheme Countries' (v7.0 May 2025, v8.0 Dec 2025) is a dated, structured artefact for tracking Montenegrin PSP scheme participation.

source_name: BIS — CPMI payment/FMI statistics portal and country payment-system information (Red Book)
why_relevant: BIS/CPMI provides the methodological standard (d168) and comparative Red Book payment statistics against which Montenegrin RTGS/DNS data published by the CBCG can be benchmarked. Montenegro is not a CPMI member so it is not in the Red Book series itself — value is methodological and comparative rather than country-specific.

source_name: World Bank — Western Balkans Regular Economic Report (financial-sector chapter)
why_relevant: Semi-annual (spring/autumn) report with a dedicated financial-sector section and a Montenegro country note; provides comparable cross-Western-Balkans framing of credit growth, NPLs, financial inclusion and regulatory reform progress in English.
